contributions.who: Dr Peter Prinsley (Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket) (Lab)
contributions.text: 15. What assessment she has made of the adequacy of the national funding formula for schools in Suffolk.
contributions.name: Dr Peter Prinsley

contributions.who: The Minister for School Standards (Georgia Gould)
contributions.text: Suffolk local authority is receiving £596 million for mainstream schools in the financial year 2026-27 through the dedicated schools grant. That represents an increase in funding of 2.8% per pupil since 2025-26.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: I am sure that the Minister is aware of the f40 campaigners, whom I had the pleasure of meeting in Parliament quite recently. The f40 campaign highlights that some local authorities receive substantially less funding per pupil than others, particularly for children with special needs. As the Minister reviews the national funding formula, will she take into account the particular difficulties of some of our schools in Suffolk?
contributions.name: Dr Peter Prinsley

contributions.text: I am very aware of the f40 group and the work that many colleagues do campaigning for their schools. The national funding formula allocates funding based on schools’ and pupils’ characteristics, including by using proxies for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities. The Department is working on changes to the national funding formula and the high-needs funding system, and we will take into account the points raised by my hon. Friend and the f40 campaigners to ensure that every area is funded. As part of our reform, a greater amount of funding from high needs will go into school budgets to support children with special educational needs.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould
